craft_claim: Ornament detached from meaning (the 'purple patch' or purple prose) draws attention to style and diminishes the whole, which is the tone's canonical failure mode.

supporting_evidence.note: Horace warns against a few brilliant passages sewn into a work for display that clash with the surrounding whole, establishing the canonical critique of ornament without function.

supporting_evidence.location: Personality and Social Psychology Review 8(4):364-382, on disfluency costs
supporting_evidence.note: Because aesthetic pleasure rises with processing ease under default conditions, piled-on ornament that impedes processing defeats the tone's own effect.

scope: All forms; most acute in long-form prose and in academic or informational writing.
exceptions: Deliberate pastiche or parody of ornamental styles, where the excess is the point.
